newsitem.title: USA: S&P says number of dividend increases rose in Q1.
newsitem.headline: S&P says number of dividend increases rose in Q1.

text.p: Standard & Poor's, a division of McGraw-Hill Cos Inc, on Tuesday said the number of companies increasing their dividends was still climbing, although that may change with higher interest rates and slackening corporate profits.
The number of dividend increases reported to S&P in the first quarter of 1997 rose nine percent to 644 from 590 in the year-earlier period, S&P said.
In March, 180 companies reported dividend increases compared with 165 in the same month of 1996. It was the sixth straight month of year-to-year improvement.
To be sure, unfavorable dividend actions have also been rising, though modestly from an historical standpoint, S&P said.

Still, corporate profits, the primary determinant of dividends, will continue to lose momentum as the economic expansion matures and interest rates rise, S&P said. That should lead to a more irregular dividend pattern, it said.
